name: Warn
summary: Shopify app from Effective Apps that adds customizable warnings (Prop 65 labels, shipping-delay alerts, age-verification and withdrawal disclaimers) to product, cart and checkout pages, as text or pop-ups, targeted globally or by product, collection, country or US state. On the App Store since December 2019.
best_for: shopify merchants who know exactly which notice they need: a Prop 65 label, a shipping-delay alert, an age-verification disclaimer, a we-no-longer-ship-here message, and want it on the right products, collections or countries without touching theme code, for $6.99 a month or nothing at all if one plain warning will do
skip_if: you are on a standard Shopify plan and specifically want the checkout blocked or a warning shown on the Checkout page: both are Plus Plan features and the Plus Plan is for Shopify Plus stores, so the capability the app's name advertises is not available to you at any price here. Also skip it if you sell off Shopify, or if what you actually need is consent and privacy management (cookie banners, consent records, data-subject requests) rather than a notice on a page.
honest_knock:
The app is called Warn: Warnings Checkout Blocks, and blocking checkout is the one thing most readers of this listing cannot buy at the advertised price. Checkout blocking, and showing a warning on the Checkout page at all, sits on the Plus Plan at $12.99 a month, and that plan says, in the App Store's own words, that it is for Shopify Plus stores. The $6.99 Premium plan says the opposite: for all stores except Shopify Plus. So the two tiers are not a small ladder and a big one, they are two different audiences, and which one you may buy is decided by your Shopify subscription rather than by how much warning you need. If you are on a standard Shopify plan and came here to stop a checkout, read the plan labels before you install.

The second thing to be clear about is what the app does and does not take off your hands. It renders the notice, targets it by product, collection or country, and styles it to your store. It does not tell you what Proposition 65, a GDPR withdrawal notice or an age-verification disclaimer has to say in your jurisdiction, and it does not keep that wording current when the rule changes. The compliance language stays your problem and your liability; this is the display layer for it.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (prices read 2026-09-20 on apps.shopify.com/product-notes) Billed in USD, every 30 days, and the ladder has three steps rather than the two the app's own summary suggests. Free gives you one textual warning across unlimited products, with the styling, per-product targeting and per-country targeting included. Premium is $6.99 a month or $41.94 a year, and the annual figure really is half of twelve monthly payments. It lifts the cap to unlimited warnings, notes and pop-ups, adds cart and checkout warnings, targeting by product or collection, and US-state geo-targeting on top of country targeting — but the plan is labelled for all stores EXCEPT Shopify Plus. Plus Plan is $12.99 a month or $77.94 a year, again exactly half of twelve monthly payments, and it is the Shopify Plus plan: the same feature list, plus warnings shown on the Checkout itself and the rule that lets a warning block checkout when configured. Both paid plans carry a 7-day free trial.

compare_with.name: Consentmo
compare_with.why: They are answers to different questions that both get filed under compliance. Consentmo is consent and privacy management: cookie banners, GDPR and CCPA consent records, data-subject requests: the paperwork side. Warn is the notice itself, placed on a product, cart or checkout page and targeted by product, collection, country or US state. If your problem is a Prop 65 label on 40 products or a shipping-delay banner for two countries, Warn is the narrower and cheaper fit at $6.99 a month. If your problem is proving what a visitor consented to, a warning app does not address it at all. The one place they meet is checkout blocking, and there Warn's answer depends on your Shopify plan rather than on the app.

claims.comparability: Dossier remark that checkout blocking is Plus only versus the Premium feature list.

claims.comparability: Monthly price times twelve versus the yearly amount on the approval screen.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Warn Product Labels on a Shopify development store: the install, a California Proposition 65 warning made from the template and active in the app, the targeting tab, a Textual Warning block with the warning ID saved in the theme editor (the display in the shop was not seen), the plan page, the Premium Yearly approval screen (not approved) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid; the saved theme change was not removed. Install: the App Store listing (English) is called Warn Product Checkout Warnings and in the admin the app is called Warn Product Labels, by Effective Apps. The install started at 15:15 and the Install app dialog asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. After Install, with no payment, the app opened straight on the plan Free with the screen Welcome to Warn Product Labels, Getting Started (Activate the App Embed, Create your first warning, Verify your setup), App embed status: Inactive and Warnings 0 of 1 used. Core action, a warning on a product page: Add a warning, the template California Proposition 65 (Textual, California) and Use this template. To go on a tick is required for: I agree that these templates are not legal advice, that Effectify LTD is not responsible for the wording I publish, and that I accept the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. The editor Add New Textual Warning has the tabs Content, Design and Targeting. The text is WARNING: This product can expose you to chemicals including [chemical name], which is known to the State of California to cause cancer and/or birth defects or other reproductive harm. For more information, visit www.P65Warnings.ca.gov. The placeholder [chemical name] stays in the text, so the shop owner has to fill in the chemical. Targeting: All products and Certain countries with US preselected; Target specific US states only is greyed out with Available on Premium. Upgrade to target specific US states. After saving, the message Warning created successfully appeared and then Setup Guide (Step 1 of 2): copy the Warning ID and paste it into the Warning ID field of the Textual Warning block in the Theme Editor; step 2 is Open Theme Editor. The list All warnings shows Proposition 65 warning, All products, Specific countries, Textual, Active, Views 0, and a banner says Everything is working. Time, approximate tester observations: about 2 minutes and 9 steps from the install to a warning that was made and active in the app; about 5 minutes and 14 steps to the block in the theme editor. Theme change: in the theme editor, on the product template, Product information, Add block, Apps, Textual Warning of Warn Product Labels was added; the field Warning ID (optional) (Leave blank to show all warnings. Enter a Warning ID to show only that warning in this block.) was filled with the warning ID and the theme test-data was saved (Changes saved.). This theme change was needed for the result and is still saved on the product The Inventory Not Tracked Snowboard. In the editor the block only shows the placeholder Textual warning will appear here. The real display in the shop was not seen: the shop has a password that was not entered, the warning targets the country US, and the App Embed was not switched on. Plans: Account Settings, Your Plan: Free, with a switch Monthly or Yearly (Save up to 50%). Only Premium is shown, no Plus plan, because the store is not on Shopify Plus. Monthly: Premium Monthly $6.99 /month (billed monthly). Yearly: SALE: SAVE 50%, Premium Yearly $3.49 /month (billed annually). The Premium features are US state targeting, Target California for Prop 65, Works on every warning type, Unlimited warnings, Country targeting, Product and collection targeting, Prevent checkout and Online support, with the button Start 7-day free trial. Deviation from the dossier: the app shows Prevent checkout as a Premium feature for this store that is not on Plus, while the dossier says that blocking the checkout is only on the Plus plan; whether it works was not tested. The managed pricing page of Shopify says No plans are available for your store, so the app bills in its own way. Checkout: Start 7-day free trial on Premium Yearly opened the Shopify Approve subscription screen: You have a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov., subtotal $41,94 plus any applicable taxes, total $41,94 due 24 Nov., Subscription details $41,94 USD every year, an Add payment method row and a greyed out Approve button. The sentence about a test charge was NOT on the screen and a payment method had to be added, so nothing was approved; no card was entered; the screen was closed with Cancel. Cancelling: no subscription ran, because the Free plan was used. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu of the app and Uninstall; the dialog Uninstall Warn Product Labels? says you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required and there is a feedback box. We gave Testing multiple apps at about 15:21 and the app left the installed list. Not tested: the paid plans and US state targeting (they need a payment method), the pop-up and the confirmation by a shopper, the checkout warning and blocking the checkout, the display on the real shop, switching on the App Embed, and whether a confirmation is stored with the order. Clean up: the warning and the saved theme change were not removed; the theme test-data still holds the block Textual Warning on the product template, now empty because the app was uninstalled; the approval screen was cancelled and nothing was paid; the app was uninstalled; all browser tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: A tick that the templates are not legal advice is needed before a template can be used; the template keeps a [chemical name] placeholder that the owner has to fill; the warning shows nothing in the theme editor but a placeholder; the setup needs a manual copy of a warning ID into a theme block; the Premium Yearly approval screen asks for a payment method and has no test charge sentence; and the app shows Prevent checkout on Premium while the dossier says it is Plus only.

friction.export_route: No export or reimport was performed; no file was downloaded or examined. The two categorised kit records were not entered; the objects tested were not kit records.

The paid plans and US state targeting, which need a payment method.
The pop-up and the confirmation by a shopper, the checkout warning and blocking the checkout.
The display on the real shop (password, country US, App Embed not switched on).
Whether a confirmation is stored with the order.
Export and reimport.
